  "text": "Mara stepped back. The water followed the slope between two floorboards, though she had never noticed a slope there before.

Their mother fetched a towel. When she bent to lay it down, the child caught her sleeve.

“Wait,” she said.

From the cupboard came a small sound, like a spoon touching the rim of a bowl. Mara opened the door. The shelves held flour, jars of beans, a sack of potatoes. Nothing moved. At the back, behind the flour, lay a wet coil of rope.

Her sister knelt beside her. “That was tied to the harbor steps,” she said. She reached for it, then drew her hand away. “I remember holding it.”

The child took the fifth spoon from the windowsill and set it inside the cupboard. She sat on the floor, close enough to see past the jars.

“I’m here,” she said.

Rainwater gathered in the bowl of the spoon. For a while they watched it fill. Then a voice, faint and hoarse, came from somewhere behind the wall.

“I know.”

Mara’s sister covered her mouth. Their mother moved the jars aside, one by one, until her fingers found a narrow gap between the boards. Cold air passed through it. Mara brought a lamp, but its light reached only as far as the rope.

The child stood and pulled on her coat. “He can’t come through this way,” she said.

Outside, the clouds were lifting. Their mother left the cupboard open, and together they went down to the harbor."
